stem: A paint shop makes a shade of paint called Sea Mist by mixing blue paint, white paint and grey paint in the ratio $2 : 9 : 4$ by volume.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the volume of white paint in 7.5 litres of Sea Mist.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Express the ratio   volume of grey paint : volume of Sea Mist   in the form $1 : n$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A decorator has 1.5 litres of blue paint, 8 litres of white paint and 2.6 litres of grey paint.
Find the greatest volume of Sea Mist she can make.

solution:
(a) Total number of parts $= 2 + 9 + 4 = 15$.
Volume of white paint $= \frac{9}{15} \times 7.5 = 4.5$ litres.

(b) Grey : Sea Mist $= 4 : 15 = 1 : \frac{15}{4} = 1 : 3.75$.

(c) Each batch of 15 parts needs 2 parts blue, 9 parts white and 4 parts grey.
Volume of one part allowed by each colour:
blue: $1.5 \div 2 = 0.75$ litres,
white: $8 \div 9 = 0.888\ldots$ litres,
grey: $2.6 \div 4 = 0.65$ litres.
The grey paint runs out first, so one part is at most $0.65$ litres.
Greatest volume of Sea Mist $= 15 \times 0.65 = 9.75$ litres.
(Check: this uses $2 \times 0.65 = 1.3$ litres of blue and $9 \times 0.65 = 5.85$ litres of white, both available.)
syllabus_check: 4052 Ratio and proportion: dividing a quantity in a given three-part ratio (a), expressing a ratio in the form 1 : n (b), and a limiting-ingredient ratio problem requiring comparison of the three available amounts (c). The two 1-mark parts use only the stem and come first; the 2-mark chain is the closer. No topic outside 4052; calculator use is routine. Marks 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 match the slot.
originality_note: Not a two-person money transfer that changes a ratio (exemplars 1 and 4), not a chained A:B, B:C ratio with a fraction moving between groups (exemplar 3), not a population table (exemplar 5; only the 'Express … in the form 1 : n' verb is borrowed, as the moderator asked). The context (a three-colour paint mixture) and the limiting-ingredient reasoning in (c) are new to this paper; nothing in paper-so-far.md uses ratio, paint or mixtures.
